questions.prompt: How autonomously should /goal execute the parity milestones?
questions.description: The plan already defines milestone gates. This decides when execution should pause for your input.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Execute autonomously through all milestones, stopping only for missing external access, destructive live-test approval, or a material scope decision not settled by the facts.

questions.prompt: What live GitHub validation resources may execution assume?
questions.description: Full parity validation needs a disposable repository and, for notification behavior, a dedicated test identity or equivalent controlled setup. Mutations must remain confined to named fixtures.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use a named disposable GitHub repository plus a dedicated test identity where needed; allow reversible fixture mutations automatically, but require explicit approval before destructive or externally visible live actions.

questions.prompt: What compatibility and release boundary should each milestone maintain?
questions.description: The work changes configuration, cache schemas, commands, and packaged binaries across several independently releasable slices.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep every milestone independently releasable: preserve existing config and cache data through additive/versioned migrations, add a changeset for user-facing behavior, and validate source, standalone binary, npm, and Homebrew paths at the final release gate.
